books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Senator Blanche K. Bruce, speech before the Senate (March 31, 1876)

stimulus.text:
“I have confidence, not only in this country and her institutions, but in the endurance, capacity, and destiny of my people. We will, as opportunity offers and ability serves, seek our places, sometimes in the field of letters, arts, sciences, and the professions. More frequently mechanical pursuits will attract and elicit our efforts; more still of my people will find employment and livelihood as the cultivators of the soil. The bulk of this people—by surroundings, habits, adaption, and choice—will continue to find their homes in the South, and constitute the masses of its yeomanry.”

—Senator Blanche K. Bruce, speech before the Senate to introduce a resolution appointing a committee to investigate election practices in Mississippi, March 31, 1876
stimulus.source_note: Senator Blanche K. Bruce, speech before the Senate, March 31, 1876. Public domain. Wording verified against the quotation in 5 Steps to a 5, AP U.S. History 2024, Chapter 16, including the book’s spelling “adaption.”

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Bruce spoke in March 1876. Within a year, the event that ended Reconstruction was

options.text: the ratification of the Fourteenth Amendment in 1868.
options.misconception: Background: the Fourteenth Amendment was ratified in 1868, eight years earlier.

options.text: the impeachment trial of Andrew Johnson in the Senate.
options.misconception: Background: Johnson’s impeachment was in 1868, and it changed nothing about Reconstruction’s end.

options.text: the Compromise of 1877 and the withdrawal of federal troops.
the founding of the Freedmen’s Bureau.
options.misconception: Background: the Bureau was founded in 1865, at Reconstruction’s start.

rationales.A: Background: the Fourteenth Amendment was ratified in 1868, eight years earlier.
rationales.B: Background: Johnson’s impeachment was in 1868, and it changed nothing about Reconstruction’s end.
rationales.C: The disputed election of 1876 left Hayes and Tilden both claiming victory. The Compromise of 1877 gave Hayes the presidency, and in return the last federal troops left the South, ending Reconstruction.
rationales.D: Background: the Bureau was founded in 1865, at Reconstruction’s start.
rationales.general:
1. Bruce spoke in March 1876, and the presidential election that November ended in dispute.
2. Background: neither Hayes nor Tilden could claim the electoral votes of three Southern states.
3. The Compromise of 1877 settled the election by giving Hayes the presidency and pulling federal troops out of the South.
4. With the troops gone, Reconstruction was over.
Remember: a disputed election can end an era, not just pick a president.
